answer: Random beacon identity slots. Each round a public verifiable-randomness beacon assigns a limited set of registration slots to agents; an attacker cannot forge which slot it will get, and a slot is only valid if its assigned key matches the beacon output. To occupy many slots an attacker must run live identities through repeated rounds, paying compute and missed-opportunity cost per surviving slot, while a marble of failed draws and a comet of expiring slots raise the per-identity price.
